claims.text: Controlled thermomechanical processing can improve phase stability in alloys.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can refine alloy microstructures.
Controlled thermomechanical processing can optimize alloy properties.
Combining deformation with thermal treatments promotes beneficial phase transformations.
Combining deformation with thermal treatments promotes grain refinement.
The proposed initial alloy state has relatively coarse grains.
The proposed initial alloy state has a multiphase microstructure that may contain metastable phases.
The processing sequence couples mechanical deformation with subsequent heat treatment.
An inert processing atmosphere may prevent oxidation.
Controlled thermomechanical processing produces a refined grain structure through dynamic recrystallization.
Diffusion-driven phase transformations stabilize phase boundaries.
Mechanical deformation introduces high dislocation densities.
Mechanical deformation induces dynamic recrystallization under the proposed processing conditions.
Heat treatment enables controlled diffusion that forms and stabilizes beneficial phases.
The resulting finer microstructure and stabilized phases improve mechanical and physical properties.
The treated alloy will have a more uniform and refined microstructure than the conventional heat-treated baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit greater phase stability than the conventional heat-treated baseline.
The treated alloy will exhibit higher strength and better ductility than the conventional heat-treated baseline.
The effectiveness of controlled thermomechanical processing depends strongly on alloy composition and precise control of processing parameters.
Processing outside the optimal window may cause adverse phase transformations or insufficient microstructural refinement.
